channel.title: 2026-08 on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in 2026-08 on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: Better tools for managing blocked users
item.description:
GitHub updated blocked-user management for personal accounts and organizations. The blocked users list now supports search, sorting, and pagination to make large lists easier to manage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: The new GitHub Copilot experience in Slack
item.description:
GitHub’s Slack integration now includes agentic GitHub Copilot capabilities from Copilot CLI and the Copilot app, available in public preview. Users can interact with @GitHub in Slack to work with these features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Shared agentic work with GitHub Copilot in Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot can now be started from Microsoft Teams by mentioning @GitHub in a channel, thread, or direct message. This creates a shared agent session that participants can view and help guide.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Stop restricting the agent. Start restricting its environment.
item.description:
Azure SRE Agent argues that AI safety is better achieved by constraining the runtime environment rather than the agent itself. This approach aims to preserve autonomy while reducing risk compared with human review or standing credentials.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Pinning saved views to the repository issues sidebar is generally available and more
item.description:
GitHub now lets you pin saved views to a repository’s issues sidebar, so frequently used views are easier to access. The feature is generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Windows 11 arm64 VS2026 image generally available
item.description:
Windows 11 arm64 images with Visual Studio 2026 are now generally available on standard and larger GitHub-hosted runners. Workflows can use the new image by updating the runner image reference.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement
item.description:
Azure Gateway now generally supports advertising summarized (aggregated) prefixes to on-premises networks instead of advertising every individual virtual network prefix. This is available for route advertisement in Azure gateways.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Copilot introduces direct access to agents
item.description:
Starting in August 2026, Azure Copilot will let customers interact directly with agents to move from questions to actions faster. Users can choose the agent best suited to their goal.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code scanning adds a mitigated alert dismissal reason
item.description:
Code scanning now supports dismissing alerts with the reason “Mitigated” when the vulnerability still exists in code but is offset by external controls, such as a web application firewall or network protections.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Separate GitHub Actions path for GitHub Code Quality
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality CodeQL Actions workflows now have a dedicated workflow path and are generally available. Run history and Actions usage reports can now distinguish GitHub Code Quality runs from other Actions workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Track GitHub Code Quality enablement changes in the audit log
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality now emits audit log events when it is enabled, disabled, or its repository settings are changed. This adds a history trail for Code Quality configuration changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.3 improves GitHub Actions queries and JavaScript modeling
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.3 adds source modeling for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Vue, and updates several GitHub Actions queries for better accuracy. It is a CodeQL release used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Databricks Lakebase in four additional regions
item.description:
Azure Databricks Lakebase is now generally available in four additional Azure regions: North Central US, France Central, Germany West Central, and East Asia. This increases deployment options and regional availability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for mid-August 2026
item.description:
Azure SQL added customizable keyboard shortcuts for Quick Queries, the Results Grid, and the Query Editor in Visual Studio Code. The changes can be configured directly in the editor.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: SQL Formatter in MSSQL extension
item.description:
The MSSQL extension now includes SQL Formatter in public preview, letting you format SQL scripts directly in the editor. It adds customizable formatting options to align scripts with a preferred coding style.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SQL Database provisioning in MSSQL extension
item.description:
Azure SQL Database provisioning in the MSSQL extension is now generally available. Users can create and connect to a managed Azure SQL Database from their editor, with ARM, Bicep, and Terraform templates included.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the Frost Radar™: Cloud Workload Protection Platforms, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a leader in the 2026 Frost Radar for Cloud Workload Protection Platforms. The post highlights Microsoft Defender for Cloud as its unified runtime security offering.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: vCore Customization: Disable Multithreading and Configurable Constrained Cores
item.description:
Azure Virtual Machines vCore Customization is now generally available. The update adds support for disabling SMT/Hyper-Threading and for configuring constrained core counts on supported VMs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: BYON (Bring Your Own NIC) in Azure Site Recovery
item.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports Bring Your Own NIC (BYON) for Azure-to-Azure test failover and failover, allowing you to attach an existing pre-provisioned NIC in the target region. This can preserve existing network configurations and reserved IP settings.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: How we built ThinkingBox to measure whether agents finish the job
item.description:
ThinkingBox splits the execution framework from the benchmark package so each can be updated independently. The article frames this as a way to measure whether agents actually finish tasks.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Track organization code quality trends
item.description:
GitHub’s organization-level Code Quality dashboard now has a Trends tab. It shows code quality changes across repositories over time instead of only a point-in-time view.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now supports enterprise managed settings. Administrators can centrally control plugin governance, MCP server access, OpenTelemetry, and permission modes across the enterprise.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Credential revocation and deauthorization by token type
item.description:
GitHub added self-service incident response actions to deauthorize and revoke user credentials by token type and by specific user. The update extends existing credential revocation workflows for security incidents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution License-included service will be retired August 30, 2027
item.description:
Azure VMware Solution license-included service will be retired on August 30, 2027. The change follows Broadcom’s updated VMware licensing policy requiring customers on hyperscaler platforms to bring their own portable VMware Cloud Foundation license.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Managed Instance on Azure App Service
item.description:
Managed Instance on Azure App Service is now generally available. It is intended to help migrate web applications from on-premises or virtual machines to Azure App Service with minimal configuration and no code changes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Ipv6 support in Azure Firewall
item.description:
Azure Firewall is now in public preview with IPv6 support. Customers can configure Azure Firewall and Firewall Policy in dual-stack mode for IPv4 and IPv6 traffic, including native IPv6 network-rule filtering and DNS Proxy support.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Hunting MacSync Stealer infrastructure through behavioral pivots
item.description:
Microsoft describes how it tracked MacSync Stealer infrastructure despite rapid domain rotation by using stable behavioral pivots. The investigation identified more than 30 related domains.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Zone redundancy for Azure SQL Managed Instance Next-gen General Purpose
item.description:
Azure SQL Managed Instance Next-gen General Purpose now supports public preview of zone redundancy. It automatically distributes compute and data across availability zones to improve resilience and business continuity.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Dragon Copilot Physician Apps and Agents on Microsoft Marketplace
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace is now a new channel for discovering, evaluating, and purchasing Dragon Copilot Physician Apps and Agents. The availability applies to Dragon Copilot customers in the United States.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: From single call to agents: five new Claude capabilities now available in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now supports five new Claude capabilities on Azure-hosted models: structured outputs, web search, web fetch, MCP connector, and tool search. The update positions a model endpoint for agent-style workflows rather than single-call usage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Linux on WSL
item.description:
Azure Linux on WSL is available in Public Preview (Beta). It lets teams run Azure Linux on developer workstations to validate production-aligned behavior, reproduce issues more reliably, and reduce debugging time.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Watch TypeScript creator Anders Hejlsberg on The Peterman Pod
item.description:
After TypeScript 7.0, Anders Hejlsberg discusses porting TypeScript from JavaScript to Go, along with the benefits and drawbacks of agentic AI for coding. The post is a podcast announcement rather than a technical changelog.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Multiple redirect URIs and token refresh for OAuth apps
item.description:
GitHub updated OAuth app and GitHub App platform support to improve app security. The changes include optional expiring access tokens with refresh tokens for OAuth apps, and support for multiple redirect URIs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Databricks Runtime 10.4 LTS will reach end of life on November 1, 2026
item.description:
Azure Databricks Runtime 10.4 LTS has already reached end of support on March 18, 2025 and will reach end of life on November 1, 2026. After that date, it will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Grok 4.6 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.6 is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot as a new reasoning model from xAI. GitHub says it is intended for agentic coding and complex multi-step workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 10
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 10 weekly release adds new models, portable plugins, and workflow improvements for agents. The updates are aimed at making Copilot more flexible across editors, the command line, and the Copilot app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Routing and Failover for Microsoft.Extensions.AI
item.description:
Microsoft.Extensions.AI adds experimental routing primitives for model/provider selection and failover: RoutingChatClient, SemanticRoutingChatClient, and FailoverChatClient. These support content-based routing, failover handling, and custom routing policies.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: License data quality improvements
item.description:
GitHub now sources license information for dependency graph software components from package registries such as npmjs.org and PyPI. This is intended to improve the accuracy and completeness of displayed license data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Block users from comments in personal repositories
item.description:
GitHub now lets you block or unblock users directly from comments on pull requests and issues in repositories owned by personal accounts. The action can be performed from the comment interface.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Who spent all the tokens? Real-time, run-scoped cost control for AI agents
item.description:
TokenOps is presented as a run-scoped cost control mechanism for AI agents that enforces a shared budget in real time. The stated goal is to stop runaway runs before costs accumulate and invoices arrive.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Control plane metrics collection for AKS with Managed Prometheus
item.description:
Control plane metrics collection for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) with Azure Monitor Managed Service for Prometheus is now generally available. It provides native observability into key managed control plane components.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Live Resize for Shared Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Data Disks
item.description:
Live Resize is now generally available for shared Premium SSD v2 and Ultra data disks. It lets you expand disk capacity dynamically without application disruption.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
item.description:
Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server are now generally available. They let you verify major version upgrade readiness before starting the upgrade.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Gemini 3.7 Flash is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is rolling out Gemini 3.7 Flash, Google’s latest Flash model. GitHub says early testing showed improvements in web and app development and agentic tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications
item.description:
Microsoft will retire the containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications on September 14, 2026. After that date, the agent will be permanently disabled and will stop sending SAP logs to Microsoft Sentinel.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: ai: From Sync APIs to support for the GPT-5 model series and agentic workflows: What’s new in Azure Content Understanding – August 2026
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding gained support for the GPT-5 model series and agentic workflows, along with Sync APIs. The release focuses on helping developers extract structured, grounded data from enterprise content across documents, forms, tables, images, audio, and video.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Azure Content Understanding GPT-5 Series Guide: Model Selection, Grounding Improvements, and Confidence Enhancements
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding is adding support for the GPT-5 series and updating grounding and confidence features. The change is intended to improve model selection flexibility, efficiency, and extraction quality across document, image, audio, and video content.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Agent Plugins 1.0 in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub published Agent Plugins 1.0, enabling a plugin to be built once and used across compatible agent clients. The release is available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app, with support announced alongside AWS, Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rule insights for organizations in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has released the rule insights dashboard in public preview for organizations. It provides a visual overview of how repository rulesets are evaluated and enforced at the organization level.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Instructions Hygiene – What Frontier Models Still Need You to Say
item.description:
The post says frontier models still need explicit, well-scoped instructions to work reliably. It emphasizes giving the right level of guidance rather than assuming the model will infer missing details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Batch rule updates for Azure Front Door
item.description:
Batch rule updates are now generally available for Azure Front Door Standard and Premium. The feature lets customers add, update, delete, or reorder multiple rules in a rule set as a single coordinated operation.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Front Door mutual TLS
item.description:
Azure Front Door now supports mutual TLS in public preview. It lets Front Door authenticate clients with X.509 certificates before forwarding requests to the application.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Markdown for Agents in Azure App Service
item.description:
Azure App Service now has a public preview of Markdown for Agents. When a client requests Markdown, App Service can automatically serve a cleaner Markdown version of app content for AI agents and other tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: aks: Release 2026-08-07
item.description:
AKS release v20260807 adds Node Auto Provisioning support for restricted publicNetworkAccess clusters, global automatic availability zone placement, control-plane-only upgrades to AKS LTS, and GA node pool rollback. It also includes several behavioral changes that can trigger immediate node reimages on Kubernetes 1.37+, plus component and image updates.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22 release candidate is now available. The post says it introduces new platform capabilities, with one highlighted change being administrator configuration for Copilot CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot memory and Ollama in GitHub Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds persistent memory, local model access via Ollama, and additional enterprise controls. The update also improves chat workflows and fixes reliability issues with MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Automatically migrate branch protection rules to repository rulesets
item.description:
GitHub now lets you convert existing branch protection rules into repository rulesets from repository settings. This provides a direct migration path to the newer policy framework.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of MAI-Code-1-Flash
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate MAI-Code-1-Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences on September 10, 2026. The suggested replacement is MAI-Code-1.1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: .NET 11 Preview 7 is now available!
item.description:
Microsoft announced .NET 11 Preview 7, covering updates across libraries, runtime, SDK, C#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, Entity Framework Core, F#, and Windows Forms. The provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: .NET and .NET Framework August 2026 servicing releases updates
item.description:
Microsoft posted a recap of the August 2026 servicing updates for .NET and .NET Framework. The provided text does not include specific version numbers, fixes, or affected components.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: MAI-Code-1.1-Flash available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
MAI-Code-1.1-Flash is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. It adds native vision support for image understanding and improves coding quality over MAI-Code-1-Flash.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: How to Pretty-Print Your Kubernetes YAML as KYAML and Why You'd Want To
item.description:
Kubernetes introduced KYAML, a strict YAML subset that uses explicit braces, brackets, quotes, and trailing commas to avoid common YAML pitfalls like indentation errors and silent type coercion. The post explains how to output or format manifests as KYAML with kubectl and yamlfmt, and notes that KYAML remains valid YAML with no new parser required.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: 2.2X IDPS performance optimization in Azure Firewall
item.description:
Azure Firewall Premium now supports up to 22 Gbps throughput with TLS inspection and IDPS in Deny mode, up from 10 Gbps. It also increases per-TCP-connection throughput with IDPS enabled in Alert or Deny mode to 600 Mbps, from 300 Mbps.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Per-model token breakdown in the usage report
item.description:
GitHub’s usage report now includes a per-model breakdown of tokens behind AI credits. The report shows token details for each model, including input, output, and cache usage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Microsoft Fabric Item Recovery will be enabled by default for tenants without an explicit setting
item.description:
Starting August 23, 2026, Microsoft Fabric Item Recovery will be enabled by default for tenants that do not already have an explicit setting configured. Supported item types will use a 3-day recovery window by default, and admins can review or change the setting.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise
item.description:
Microsoft says it was named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for MDR/MXDR for the Enterprise. The post highlights Microsoft Defender Experts MDR as combining AI, threat intelligence, and human expertise.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: DeadLock ransomware: Breaking down a Rust-based encryptor with decentralized recovery infrastructure
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes DeadLock ransomware as a financially motivated operation using a Rust-based encryptor and decentralized infrastructure for victim communications, negotiations, and data leak operations. The group uses double extortion to pressure victims.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Copilot on web expands conversation controls
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot Chat on github.com with new conversation controls to make the web experience easier to use. The changes include quicker access to recent chats and the ability to minimize the chat panel.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub billing in India now supports automatic recurring payments
item.description:
GitHub billing in India now supports automatic recurring payments for monthly and annual bills when using eligible saved credit cards. The change uses a payment mandate for recurring charges.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Custom thread subscriptions are being deprecated
item.description:
GitHub is deprecating custom thread subscription settings for notifications. Users will no longer be able to configure them, and support for existing custom thread subscription settings will be removed.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — August 3
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s August 3 weekly release notes mention updates across the desktop app, CLI, and VS Code focused on resuming and organizing work, reviewing changes, and asking questions without losing context. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprises can now install third-party GitHub Apps
item.description:
Enterprise owners can now install public GitHub Apps built outside their enterprise on enterprise accounts. This enables third-party integrations for enterprise management scenarios.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard adds a return on investment section
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes a “Potential return on investment” section. It links Copilot spend to pull request output to help estimate ROI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review effort levels are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review effort levels are now generally available. Lite and Balanced let you choose review depth based on the complexity and risk of the code change.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot usage metrics API adds agent app activity
item.description:
The Copilot usage metrics API now includes activity from agent apps used in GitHub workflows. This extends usage reporting to agents from partners such as Claude and Codex.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: “Relates to” issue relationship in public preview and multi-select fields is generally available
item.description:
GitHub added a new public preview issue relationship called “Relates to” for connecting related work, and multi-select fields are now generally available for GitHub Projects.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: 🌿 Agent Terrarium: Bringing AI agents to life
item.description:
A weekend open-source desktop companion app, Agent Terrarium, explores a more interactive, less purely transactional way to work with AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Secret scanning coverage updates
item.description:
GitHub updated secret scanning coverage by adding more secrets to push protection, onboarding a new secret scanning partner, and including richer metadata in alerts. The post also notes the Secret Scanning Partnership Program now includes Lovable Labs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard
item.description:
Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard is in public preview for ExpressRoute virtual network gateways. A new resiliency model property lets you declare whether a gateway is for single-homed or multi-homed configurations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Code Quality no longer adds Copilot as a reviewer
item.description:
Enabling GitHub Code Quality on a repository no longer creates a ruleset that automatically requests GitHub Copilot as a reviewer on pull requests. Existing repositories with that ruleset are affected only if they already have it configured.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed settings to centrally control which MCP servers GitHub Copilot clients can run. Enterprise owners can now use allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers to allowlist or block specific MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Set pull request limits at the organization level
item.description:
GitHub now supports setting pull request limits at the organization level. These limits control how many open pull requests a user without write access can have.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure Databricks Genie One and Genie Agents Free Usage Extended Through January 31, 2027
item.description:
Azure Databricks Genie One and Genie Agents free usage in Azure Databricks has been extended through January 31, 2027. During the promotional period, budget controls do not apply to these products.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Kimi K3 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub has resumed rolling out Kimi K3 in GitHub Copilot. The model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Test reporting in Microsoft.Testing.Platform: from red build to root cause
item.description:
Microsoft.Testing.Platform adds test reporting that surfaces failures in GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps, uses pipeline history to distinguish regressions from flaky tests, and keeps reports usable even if the test host crashes.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Migrate from AWS FSx for Windows File Server to Azure Files with Azure Storage Mover
item.description:
Azure Storage Mover now supports preview agentless, cloud-to-cloud migration from AWS FSx for Windows File Server (SMB) to Azure Files (SMB). This lets users move Windows file shares from FSx to Azure Files without deploying or managing a migration agent.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SharePoint Connector for Azure Databricks
item.description:
The SharePoint connector for Azure Databricks is now generally available. It can be used through Lakeflow Connect to ingest files from SharePoint into Azure Databricks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Unity AI Gateway on Azure Databricks
item.description:
Unity AI Gateway is now generally available on Azure Databricks. It provides centralized governance for AI models, agents, tools, and MCP services, with controls for monitoring usage, managing costs, applying guardrails, and enforcing access control.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ​​Microsoft named a Leader in the KuppingerCole Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP)
item.description:
Microsoft says KuppingerCole named it a Leader in the Leadership Compass for Cloud Native Application Protection Platforms (CNAPP). The provided excerpt does not include technical changes or product updates beyond that recognition.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: From open lures to cloaked gates: How a macOS ClickFix campaign learned to hide
item.description:
Microsoft describes a macOS ClickFix campaign that changed from openly delivering infostealer lures to placing them behind a browser-fingerprinting gate. The shift reduces visibility of the malicious infrastructure but also creates new detection opportunities for defenders.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Explicit proxy in Azure Firewall
item.description:
Azure Firewall explicit proxy is now generally available. It lets customers configure applications and browsers to send HTTP and HTTPS traffic directly to Azure Firewall through proxy settings, instead of relying on route-based traffic forwarding.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Nested confidential (cc_v5) VMs will be retired on September 1, 2026
item.description:
Azure will retire the cc_v5 confidential VM series on September 1, 2026. After that date, the affected VM sizes will no longer be available for use or purchase, and any impacted VM not resized beforehand will be deallocated.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ChainDrop supply chain compromise: Anatomy of a self-propagating worm
item.description:
Microsoft describes ChainDrop, a credential-stealing worm embedded in 400+ compromised npm packages that spread by republishing malicious updates across software ecosystems. The post outlines the attack chain, affected environments, and guidance for detection, hunting, and remediation.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: dotnet: Beyond Chat: live Speech-to-Text with Foundry Local and C#
item.description:
The post shows how to build a live speech-to-text app in C# using Foundry Local and a compact Nemotron model. It also covers local model lifecycle management.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Customize code scanning default setup at scale
item.description:
GitHub added a new repository property, github-codeql-config-file, that lets you apply a custom configuration file to code scanning default setup. This gives you control over how CodeQL runs on repositories at scale.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Retiring the Copilot Billing Preview app
item.description:
GitHub has retired the Copilot Billing Preview app and it is no longer available. Copilot spend can now be reviewed and managed directly in GitHub billing settings.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Perimeter link feature in network security perimeter
item.description:
Microsoft Azure added a public preview of Perimeter link (cross-perimeter connectivity) for network security perimeter. It lets trusted resources in different perimeters communicate securely using Managed Identity (MSI) without adding extra network access rules.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
item.description:
Microsoft says it is expanding its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance aimed at securing AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The post highlights a broader security approach for AI and related development workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Private Link support over IPv6
item.description:
Azure Private Link now supports IPv6 in public preview. IPv6 private endpoints can be used from IPv6 clients in an Azure virtual network to privately access Azure PaaS services such as Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: 128 Seconds to disruption: Microsoft Defender stops ransomware at QNET
item.description:
Microsoft Defender isolated a compromised QNET endpoint in 128 seconds, interrupting a multi-stage ransomware attack before the payload could persist or spread.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure DNS enables DNS-based load balancing through Traffic Manager integration
item.description:
Azure DNS now supports direct integration with Azure Traffic Manager for DNS-based traffic routing in preview. This lets you associate an Azure DNS record set with a Traffic Manager profile without creating a CNAME to the trafficmanager.net domain.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network routing appliance
item.description:
Azure Virtual Network routing appliance is now generally available. It provides private connectivity across virtual networks using specialized hardware designed for low latency, high throughput, and improved performance versus virtual machines.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of GitHub Spark on github.com
item.description:
GitHub Spark will stop accepting new users and new app creation starting August 4, 2026. Existing users can keep using Spark until August 31, 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize Dependabot pull request branch names
item.description:
Dependabot now supports custom pull request branch names through new pull-request-branch-name settings in .github/dependabot.yml. You can configure a prefix, maximum length, and separators for segments and words.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage automatic enablement in Code Quality settings
item.description:
GitHub added a new Code Quality setting that can automatically generate a code coverage workflow with AI. The change is meant to reduce setup time for coverage in repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.26.2 adds Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.26.2 has been released with support for Swift 6.3.3 and Kotlin 2.4.10. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Customize the reasoning level for Copilot cloud agent
item.description:
GitHub Copilot cloud agent now lets you set the reasoning level for supported models when delegating a task. This gives you control over how much reasoning the agent uses for a request.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise team specialization for managed settings
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now apply managed settings using itemized configuration files targeted at enterprise teams. This lets large organizations delegate more specific governance without routing every change through central admins or relying on a single global configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Trusted Launch as Default
item.description:
Trusted Launch as Default is now generally available for new Azure Gen2 virtual machines and virtual machine scale sets. It automatically enables Secure Boot and vTPM for supported deployments.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Trigger Copilot automations with comments
item.description:
GitHub now supports triggering Copilot cloud agent automations from new issue comments and pull request comments. This enables comment-based workflows such as generating documentation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Strengthening NuGet Supply Chain Security: Reducing API Key Lifetime
item.description:
NuGet API key lifetimes will be reduced to 30 days starting August 17, with the goal of improving supply chain security.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Triage role can bypass issue creation restrictions
item.description:
GitHub changed issue creation restrictions so users with the triage role can now create issues in repositories where issue creation is limited to collaborators only. Previously, only users with write access could create issues under that setting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Immutability to the most recent seven days of backups on Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
item.description:
Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance now automatically apply immutability to the most recent seven days of backups. The feature is enabled by default for all databases, regardless of the configured point-in-time restore retention.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Migrate from GitLab to GitHub with GitHub Enterprise Importer
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Importer now generally supports self-serve migrations from gitlab.com and GitLab Self-Managed to GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The feature is available through GEI and the GitHub CLI.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Gateway API v1.6: TCPRoute and UDPRoute Graduate to Standard
item.description:
Gateway API v1.6.0 promotes TCPRoute and UDPRoute to Standard/v1, adding GA-level raw TCP and UDP routing. It also moves experimental APIs into a separate gateway.networking.x-k8s.io group with X-prefixed kinds to make the experimental boundary explicit.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog
